chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you intend to enter the state of Ihram outside the time of a mandatory prayer, pray two rak'ahs and then enter Ihram after them, because the meaning in the first narration is one of excellence and preference, and this narration is understood as referring to the minimum amount of prayer sufficient for entering Ihram.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the proper procedure for entering Ihram if it is not during the time of a mandatory prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration to resolve the apparent discrepancy between reports describing the pre-Ihram prayer as recommended (mustahabb) versus obligatory (wajib) by distinguishing between the ideal, virtuous practice and the minimum legal sufficiency (aqall ma yujzi). This reflects the Shia juristic principle of reconciling conflicting narrations through contextual interpretation (ta'wil), ensuring that pilgrims meet the essential requirement while acknowledging the higher spiritual merit of additional devotion.
